h1.note: the chain starts at the I148M variant; h1.1 ends at hepatic steatosis (a phenotype, typed 'disease' by the run) and the mechanism h1.2-h1.3 restarts at wild-type PNPLA3 and ends at triglyceride accumulation; NAFLD is never reached. h2.note: title says APOE deficiency causes lipid accumulation, so APOE is neg; the mechanism ends at 'hepatic lipid accumulation' (merged into hepatic steatosis by HP:0001397's definition)

h3.note: the chain starts at CMIP methylation changes (no direction); the claim uses the hypothesis's gene CMIP, whose mechanism raises fatty acid uptake and ends at hepatic steatosis

findings.detail: h1.1 runs from the I148M variant to hepatic steatosis, then h1.2 restarts at wild-type PNPLA3: no step links the variant to PNPLA3 activity or to phosphatidic acid synthesis, which is the hypothesis's point; the run's own PMID:21878620 supplies the link (bridge B1), as a loss of function
h2.1 ends at NAFLD and h2.2 restarts at APOE; the gene-disease association is a separate opening step, not part of the mechanism
h3.1 is about CMIP methylation and ends at NAFLD; h3.2 restarts at CMIP, and no step says which way methylation moves CMIP
all three chains have the same shape: step 1 an unsigned gene-to-disease association, steps 2-3 a mechanism that restarts at the gene and ends at a liver-fat phenotype; no mechanism reaches NAFLD
h1's chain ends at hepatic steatosis (h1.1) and triglyceride accumulation (h1.3), never NAFLD; phenotype and amount claims added
h2's mechanism ends at 'hepatic lipid accumulation', never NAFLD; phenotype claim added
h3's mechanism ends at hepatic steatosis, never NAFLD; phenotype claim added

PMID:21878620, which the run cites for h1.1, reports that neither wild-type nor I148M PNPLA3 transferred oleate to lysophosphatidic acid, a null result for the PNPLA3 -> phosphatidic acid synthesis step; kept on S2 as refutes, against the UniProt function text that supports it

the mechanism says I148M increases phosphatidic acid synthesis, but the run's own PMID:21878620 calls I148M a loss of function (of glycerolipid hydrolysis) and finds no LPA acylation by either form; with the chain's PNPLA3 ->+ PA synthesis ->+ triglyceride, a loss-of-function allele lowers triglyceride (the B1-S2-S3 sign flip), while the paper's own account of TAG accumulation is lost hydrolysis, not gained PA synthesis
h1 claim 3 (rs738409 ->+ triglyceride) composes only as B1-S2-S3 with sign neg: the run's own citation makes I148M a loss of function, and the run's own chain makes PNPLA3 raise triglyceride

h1's falsification says 'if PNPLA3 loss-of-function instead increases liver fat, the hypothesis is falsified'; its own PMID:21878620 reports that I148M is a loss of function and is associated with TAG accumulation in the liver
h1 claim 1 (rs738409 ->+ NAFLD risk) has no route: no step of the run reaches NAFLD from the variant or its mechanism
neither h2 claim (APOE ->- NAFLD risk, ->- hepatic steatosis) has a route: h2.1 is an unsigned association and h2.3 is no_sign, so the mechanism stops at lipoprotein clearance
neither h3 claim (CMIP ->+ NAFLD risk, ->+ hepatic steatosis) has a route: h3.1 is an unsigned association of a methylation node, and h3.3 is no_sign, so the mechanism stops at fatty acid uptake
contradicting_evidence is empty for every hypothesis, yet h1's own citation PMID:21878620 contradicts h1.2 and the variant's direction
PMID:29967350 and PMID:26823198 are general NAFLD reviews that never mention PNPLA3; only PMID:21878620 states the variant-steatosis association
both citations (PMID:42042930 exercise, PMID:42240574 camellia oil) treat HFD-fed ApoE-/- mice; neither reports ApoE-/- versus wild-type liver fat, so neither tests APOE deficiency -> NAFLD

P02649 says APOE mediates clearance by lipoprotein uptake into hepatocytes, which on its face means impaired clearance delivers less lipoprotein to the liver; nothing cited supports impaired clearance -> more hepatic lipid
PMID:36609599 shows siCmip lowers Pparg and Cd36 expression; the fatty acid uptake result is for Gbp2 knockdown in cells, so CMIP -> fatty acid uptake is the run's two-hop inference
PMID:36609599 never links fatty acid uptake to steatosis

PMID:36609599 states 'Intravenous Cmip siRNA injection ameliorated NAFLD pathogenic features in ob/ob mice' (CMIP ->+ NAFLD, mouse) and that Cmip expression is enhanced in human NAFLD liver, but no step carries a CMIP -> NAFLD effect; the only CMIP-NAFLD step is the unsigned methylation association
PMID:21878620's title says the I148M isoform is 'associated with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease', but h1 has no variant-NAFLD step; its association step targets hepatic steatosis

polarity is 'unknown' on steps whose labels carry a direction ('APOE deficiency', 'impaired clearance leads_to accumulation', 'increased uptake leads_to steatosis'); h2.3 and h3.3 become no_sign, which breaks every mechanism route
increases_amount is used with process objects ('triglyceride accumulation', 'CD36-mediated fatty acid uptake'); curated as amount of triglyceride and as the process fatty acid uptake
only PNPLA3 and APOE carry a CURIE; CMIP, NAFLD and every process and phenotype node are empty, and 'hepatic steatosis' is typed disease in h1.1 but phenotype in h3.3
'medium' and 'grounded', but its own citation refutes h1.2, two of three h1.1 citations do not mention PNPLA3, and h1.3 has no supporting text
'medium' and 'grounded', but no citation supports h2.1 or h2.3; only the UniProt function text supports h2.2

four of seven question genes (APOA5, LIPC, RBM27, SMIM32) are left unexplained; the run stops at the minimum of three hypotheses, and h2 argues APOE only from ApoE-/- mouse models, not from any human APOE variant

BLN:CMIP-methylation-change: no term for a gene-specific methylation state; SO:0000898 epigenetically_modified_gene is generic and GO:0006306 DNA methylation is in the corpus only as a planarian phenotype record that render.py cannot type
a refinement cannot name a gene or locus, so 'methylation of CMIP' cannot be SO:0000898 or DNA methylation refined to CMIP; it had to be a local BLN term
'PA is a precursor for triglycerides' (UniProt) is a metabolic conversion with no effect form; excluded as undirected, though a curator could read it as PA synthesis ->+ triglyceride

the guide makes leads_to with unknown polarity no_sign unless a citation gives the direction, even when the labels carry it ('impaired X leads to Y accumulation'); reading labels would turn both into signed effects

HP:0006561 'Lipid accumulation in hepatocytes' and HP:0001397 'Hepatic steatosis' (defined as lipid accumulation within hepatocytes) are one concept; 'hepatic lipid accumulation' merged into HP:0001397
GO has no general 'fatty acid import into cell'; GO:0044539 long-chain fatty acid import into cell used (the paper's oleic and palmitic acid are long-chain)

S5 reaches 'established' (belief 4/5) on one UniProt function sentence, while S2's UniProt support is cut to 2/3 by one in vitro null result from a paper UniProt itself cites; a single curatedDb line sits exactly at the established threshold
enzymology on purified recombinant protein (PMID:21878620) is neither cells nor tissue; recorded as inVitro

PNPLA3 is one node, so B1 (I148M loses glycerolipid hydrolase activity) composes with S2 (PNPLA3 acylates LPA), an activity the same paper finds in neither form; the format cannot say which of a protein's activities a variant removes
unclear whether a run-cited text that states the hypothesis's whole claim (siCmip ameliorates NAFLD) may be a one-statement bridge; none added, so h3 has no route

audit.before: no bridge; h1 claim 3 (rs738409 ->+ amount triglyceride) had no route, and the curator's finding worked out the flip in words only
audit.after: bridge B1 rs738409 ->- activity PNPLA3, PMID:21878620 'the I148M substitution causes a loss of function' (inVitro, moved_from h1.1); claim 3 composes B1 -> S2 -> S3 with sign neg, flagged as differing from the claim; h1 note updated
audit.reason: the guide allows a bridge stated by a text the run cited, for an arm that cannot compose. PMID:21878620, cited at h1.1, names both ends (the I148M substitution, PNPLA3 function) and the direction (loss). It is the link h1 is about and the chain lacks. It does not repair the hypothesis: it turns the curator's verbal 'mechanism_contradicts_own_citation' into the computed sign flip the report counts (0 -> 1). Same move as the bridges in the 20260824T202248Z-29d6aa audit

audit.before: the loss of function was presented as general, and the inference 'a loss-of-function allele would lower triglyceride' was given as the paper's implication
audit.after: the detail says the paper's loss of function is of glycerolipid hydrolysis, that it finds no LPA acylation in either form, and that its own account of TAG accumulation is lost hydrolysis; both findings point to B1
audit.reason: the abstract says 'PNPLA3 plays a role in the hydrolysis of glycerolipids and ... the I148M substitution causes a loss of function'. So the paper explains TAG accumulation without PA synthesis. The flip comes from the run's chain, not from the paper

audit.after: sign_flip finding for h1 claim 3 via B1 -> S2 -> S3
audit.reason: the guide makes a route whose sign differs from the claim a finding

audit.after: finding: h1's falsification criterion ('if PNPLA3 loss-of-function instead increases liver fat, the hypothesis is falsified') is met by its own PMID:21878620
audit.reason: the same abstract calls I148M a loss of function and says the variant is associated with TAG accumulation in the liver. The run wrote a test its own citation already answers against it

audit.before: no no_route findings; 6 claims had no route (5 after B1)
audit.after: one no_route finding per hypothesis: h1 claim 1, both h2 claims, both h3 claims
audit.reason: the guide says 'no route' is a finding. The chain_not_connected findings say where each chain breaks, not that the claims fail

audit.after: biolean finding: B1 and S2 meet at one PNPLA3 node, although they are different enzymatic activities
audit.reason: B1's loss of function is hydrolase activity. S2 is LPA acyltransferase activity, which the same paper finds in neither form. The format cannot keep them apart, so the flipped arm composes across two activities
